project: RAG vs Fine-Tuning vs Hybrid — CSULB Graduate Center assistant
scope: documentation synthesis only; no training, inference, evaluation, or implementation

project_overview.problem_statement: Build a factual assistant for the CSULB Graduate Center master's programs and determine, under controlled conditions, whether retrieval (RAG), small-data LoRA fine-tuning, or their hybrid best answers program questions grounded in official content.
project_overview.motivation: RAG and fine-tuning are commonly proposed as alternatives for domain adaptation; teams need evidence on which to invest in when institutional knowledge is factual and updatable and the supervised set is small.
research_questions: Does Pure RAG perform well on grounded factual QA?
Can small-data LoRA fine-tuning replace retrieval as the knowledge source?
Does a Hybrid (RAG + fine-tuned adapter) improve over Pure RAG?
What role does retrieval grounding play relative to model weights?
When is fine-tuning the appropriate tool?
goals: One frozen knowledge corpus, one frozen benchmark, one evaluation pipeline shared by all tracks.
Three controlled conditions: A=Pure RAG, B=Fine-Tuned-only, C=Hybrid.
Reproducible, checksum-guarded artifacts at every phase.
project_overview.experimental_design: Between-tracks comparison holding corpus, benchmark, scoring, and 7B base model family constant. Track A grounds a base model on retrieved chunks; Track B fine-tunes a LoRA adapter with no retrieval; Track C reuses Track A retrieval + the Track B adapter. Deterministic greedy decoding; substring/set scoring (no LLM judge).

methodology.knowledge_corpus: Frozen projection of 12 master's programs into canonical program records; source-guarded.
methodology.retrieval: Chroma persistent collection masters_track_a_v1, cosine, top_k=4, threshold=0.0.
methodology.fine_tuning: MLX-LM LoRA on mlx-community/Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct-4bit; rank 16, scale 20, dropout 0.05, 16 layers, LR 1e-4, 200 iters; best checkpoint by validation loss = iter 40 (val 1.018); 23.069M trainable params (0.303%).
methodology.ft_dataset: 121 train / 13 validation SFT examples (seed-42 split), built from the frozen corpus only (no benchmark leakage).
methodology.benchmark: 84 frozen cases across 8 categories (admissions, application, contact, multi_field, overview, retrieval_challenge, source_missing, unknown); answerable + source-missing.
methodology.evaluation_pipeline: Track-agnostic ResponseRecord scoring: answer accuracy, hallucination/abstention, citation & retrieval precision/recall, derived refusal/unsupported/completeness, latency; deterministic, unchanged across A/B/C.
methodology.controlled_comparisons: Same benchmark checksum and scoring for all tracks; each track's recompute reproduces its frozen report exactly.

track_a.architecture: question -> embed -> Chroma top-k -> grounded prompt -> base LLM -> answer + citations; refuses when no evidence.
strengths: Safe failure: abstains not fabricates (hallucination 0.16, abstention 0.84)
Fluent grounded answers with citable chunks
weaknesses: Over-abstains when retrieval misses (refusal 0.5714; 31 answerable abstentions)
track_a.key_finding: Retrieval grounding yields correct, safely-abstaining answers; retrieval recall (0.5593) is the ceiling.

track_b.architecture: question -> base + Track B LoRA -> answer (parametric knowledge only).
weaknesses: Degenerate generation: repetition, corrupted refusals, invented tokens
track_b.key_finding: 121-example LoRA injected no reliable knowledge and degraded fluency (val loss diverged after iter 40); fine-tuning did not replace retrieval.

track_c.purpose: Hybrid: Track A retrieval + Track B adapter.
track_c.architecture: question -> frozen Track A retrieval -> grounded prompt -> base + Track B LoRA -> answer + citations; empty-retrieval abstains.
strengths: Grounding + citations restored vs Track B (citation_recall 0->0.5593)
Same retrieval recall as Track A (0.5593)
weaknesses: Lowest accuracy (0.0169) — below even Track B
Adapter does not copy grounded facts into the answer
track_c.key_finding: With IDENTICAL retrieval to Track A (retrieval_recall 0.5593 for both), Track C scored 0.0169 vs 0.4576 — the context-free/overfit adapter is the binding constraint; bolting it onto RAG did not help and hurt.

research_answers.pure_rag_performed_well: Relatively yes within scope: best of the three (0.4576 accuracy, 0.16 hallucination, 0.84 abstention accuracy); absolute accuracy still bounded by retrieval recall.
research_answers.small_data_lora_replaced_retrieval: No. Track B 0.0678 vs Track A 0.4576; it fabricated on all source-missing cases and degenerated.
research_answers.hybrid_improved_over_rag: No. Track C 0.0169 < Track A 0.4576, and even < Track B 0.0678 on accuracy; the reused adapter capped quality.
research_answers.role_of_retrieval_grounding: Dominant. Identical retrieval (0.5593 recall) under A and C produced 0.4576 vs 0.0169 accuracy — the generator, not the evidence, decided the outcome.
research_answers.when_finetuning_appropriate: As a behaviour/format layer trained ON the retrieval-augmented setting, not as a knowledge store; a weak, context-free adapter provides no hybrid benefit.

central_conclusion: Within the scope of this study, retrieval grounding is the dominant factor for factual, updatable QA. Small-data LoRA neither replaced retrieval nor improved a RAG pipeline; a context-free overfit adapter degraded generation even when supplied with correct evidence. Fine-tuning is valuable only as a behaviour layer trained for the grounded setting.
